rationale: Credential and token helpers handle secrets at rest and in transit; vibe-coded leakage paths are the single most-reported AI failure class (Veracode 2026).
Modules that spawn subprocesses with caller-supplied arguments; injection of unsanitized input is the canonical attack surface.
Hashing, signing, and crypto-primitive helpers; choice of algorithm and key handling are non-obvious and frequently mis-reached-for from training memory.
Identity / attestation gates that decide who is allowed to attest, complete, or audit a brief; these enforce human-presence semantics that the GHI #290 closure pinned.
Modules issuing HTTP/network egress to external services; these cross trust boundaries and require timeout, TLS, and response-validation discipline.
Append-only ledger writers and proof helpers; the ledger is gzkit's system-of-record and any non-monotonic write corrupts every downstream audit.
ARB receipt emission, validation, and canonical-command policy; receipts are the attestation evidence chain and fabrication anywhere in the chain breaks every claim that cites a receipt.
Modules that read, store, or transmit secrets; AI-generated code hard-codes credentials at twice the human-authored rate (Veracode 2026).

YAML / JSON / arbitrary-frontmatter loaders that read operator-supplied content; unsafe loaders execute attacker-controlled payloads, and gzkit's discipline mandates ``yaml.safe_load`` and Pydantic validation at every boundary.
